# Tencent Holdings (TCEHY) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 031 | Published 2020-08-30 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-8-30/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/031.json)

Tencent growth meets political and valuation risks.

Tencent grew substantially but the end 2022 price scenario failed badly. Regulatory risks were recognized, yet the optimistic scale comparison relied too heavily on population and US analogies. The macro section correctly anticipated delayed tightening but misstated the formal inflation target and 2019 rate direction, then wrongly expected yield control.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 031-C01

**Falling claims imply reemployment**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US jobs |
| Source blocks | 10, 11 |
| Thesis family | ui-exits-not-all-jobs |

A reduction in claims does not establish that the same number returned to work: eligibility expiry, reporting changes and program transfers also reduce counts. GAO identified counting problems, so the asserted inference overstates what this indicator measures.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [COVID-19 oversight report](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-21-265/index.html) | GAO | 2021-01-28 | Verified in the audit

GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

### 031-C05

**Fed target is core-PCE ceiling**

| Field | Assessment |

The official goal is total PCE inflation and was already explicitly symmetric, not a hard ceiling. Core inflation is monitored as a signal but is not the formal target.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [June monetary report and prior strategy](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/2020-06-mpr-summary.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-06-12 | Verified in the audit

The reprinted January 2019 strategy identifies total PCE inflation, not core PCE, as the 2% target and explicitly calls the objective symmetric.

### 031-C07

**Fed tolerates next inflation overshoot**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | next inflation upswing |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US monetary policy |
| Source blocks | 50, 51, 57, 62 |
| Thesis family | average-inflation-target-overshoot |

The policy statement explicitly permitted moderate overshooting, and hikes began only in March 2022 after inflation had risen. This verifies delayed tightening, not unlimited accommodation.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: next inflation upswing

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [New policy framework](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/powell20200827a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-08-27 | Verified in the audit

Powell announced flexible average inflation targeting and employment-shortfall language; moderate overshooting after undershooting was intended, without a mechanical averaging formula.

- [March 2022 rate increase](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20220316a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2022-03-16 | Verified in the audit

The first post-pandemic increase set 0.25-0.50%, acknowledged elevated inflation and anticipated further increases and balance-sheet reduction.

### 031-C08

**Normal monetary tools cannot inflate**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Inflation mechanism |
| Source blocks | 61, 63, 64, 66 |
| Thesis family | fiscal-versus-monetary-inflation |

Fiscal transfers differ from asset swaps, but normal monetary tools also affect borrowing, exchange rates, demand and expectations. Inability to guarantee inflation at the zero bound is not the same as having no ability to raise it.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [June monetary report and prior strategy](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/2020-06-mpr-summary.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-06-12 | Verified in the audit

The reprinted January 2019 strategy identifies total PCE inflation, not core PCE, as the 2% target and explicitly calls the objective symmetric.

- [How money is created](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/how-is-money-created) | Bank of England | 2019-10-01 | Verified in the audit

Reserves are electronic central-bank settlement money. Capital is a separate resource that absorbs loan-default losses; both liquidity and capital constraints apply to banks.

### 031-C09

**Yield control keeps rates suppressed**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | next inflation cycle |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | probably |
| Asset or variable | Treasury yields |
| Source blocks | 62, 66 |
| Thesis family | treasury-yield-cap-2020s |

The Fed instead tightened and reduced holdings, with ten-year yields reaching 4.98% and positive real yields in 2023. No formal yield cap was adopted in this cycle.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: next inflation cycle

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [July 2023 FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20230726a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2023-07-26 | Verified in the audit

Federal funds target increased to 5.25-5.50%; Treasury/MBS holdings continued to decline. This was tightening rather than a permanent low-rate cap.

- [Ten-year Treasury yield](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) | Federal Reserve via FRED | Verified in the audit

Ten-year nominal Treasury yield reached 4.98% October 19, 2023; ten-year real yield (DFII 10) reached 2.52% October 25. No 1-2.5% nominal ceiling persisted.

- [July 2020 FOMC minutes](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20200729.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-08-19 | Verified in the audit

Most participants discussing yield caps/targets judged benefits modest in the prevailing environment. The committee maintained guidance and purchases without adopting explicit Treasury yield-curve control.

The subsequent broad relief act passed Congress December 21 and was signed December 27, 2020, after the election rather than during summer.

- [Second economic impact payments](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm1224) | US Treasury / IRS | 2020-12-29 | Verified in the audit

Second-round payments began in late December, up to $600 per eligible individual and qualifying child; the next round of direct checks occurred, with substantial timing delay.
